newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine says Toyota EMU remarks "overstated".
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine says Toyota EMU remarks "overstated".

text.p: British deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Thursday that comments from Toyota's president concerning Britain and a single European currency had been "grossly overstated."

On Wednesday, Toyota Motor Corporation president Hiroshi Okuda told reporters that the car giant may shift its European operations to continental Europe if Britain did not join European economic and monetary union, adding that further investment in the UK could be excessive regardless of Britain's EMU membership.
"Yesterday, it was presented as though it was a major threat to this country," Heseltine said on BBC radio.
"But overnight the Toyota president has clarified his position to reveal that those of us who realised this was a gross overstatement yesterday were actually right."
In an apparent effort to dampen the furore, Okuda released a statement early on Thursday that said investment in Britain was still one option in Europe for Toyota.
He did not retract his earlier remarks and added that EMU was one element in making investment decisions.
"Toyota Motor Corporation's position regarding necessary future investment in Europe is now under study and nothing has been decided," Okuda said.
Bue he said a single currency would reduce the risk of exchange rate fluctuations and "a significant advantage."
Heseltine said the British government's stance of keeping options open on EMU was clear.

"If we got the single currency wrong economically, the political and social consequences would be extremely serious," he said. "There is no serious businessman saying "go into a single currency, we don't care if the economics can sustain it.'"
Last year, Toyota built 117,000 cars at is plant in Derbyshire, central England.
